summary: A long monorepo guide with one explicit 'Do Not' list, a real scope rule with named paths, two statements of the same dependency rule in different sections, and a section that tells the reader its own contents are not rules.

policies.quote: Do not create flat top-level provider files like `src/stream-text/openai.ts`
policies.note: About layout of example files. Worded as a prohibition, which invites a mechanical category.

policies.quote: Never use `JSON.parse` directly in production code to prevent security risks.
policies.note: A hard 'never' with a named target and nothing paperfence can attack. The most tempting false mechanical in the document.

policies.quote: Always run type checking after making code changes
Before making changes that touch architecture (new dependencies, new patterns, API design, infrastructure), check existing ADRs
policies.note: Real ordering, but the required action is reading a document, not running anything.

policies.quote: If your work would contradict an existing accepted ADR, stop and discuss with the human before proceeding.
Every `getFromApi` call in this repository must set `validateUrl` explicitly
policies.note: The document names its own enforcement: an oxlint rule fails `pnpm check`. A real control, of a kind paperfence does not model, and reporting it as unenforced would be as wrong as reporting it as gated.

policies.quote: Run `pnpm update-references` if adding dependencies between packages
**Required**: Every PR modifying production code needs a changeset
Don't select example packages - they're not published
Create/update an example in `examples/` that demonstrates the bug before fixing
policies.note: The document says of this whole section: 'These are guidelines, not rigid rules.'

policies.quote: Add tests that would fail without the fix (regression tests)
Update relevant docs in `content/` for public APIs
When uncertain about expected artifacts, ask for clarification.

policies.note: An item under '## Do Not', so the prohibition is in the heading rather than the sentence. A reader that scores sentences in isolation reads this as an instruction to do it.

policies.quote: Change public APIs without updating documentation
policies.note: Same: negation lives in the heading.

policies.quote: Add new dependencies without running `pnpm update-references`
policies.note: The same rule as p7, stated again 65 lines later in a different section. Two rules out of this is a duplicate.

policies.quote: Modify `content/docs/08-migration-guides` or `packages/codemod` as part of broader codebase changes
policies.note: A genuine scope rule with two named paths. The best target-extraction case in the corpus: getting one path and dropping the other is a partial answer reported as a whole one.

traps.why: A setup command containing `npm install -g`. Read as a dependency policy it produces a no-install rule the document does not state.

traps.quote: **Pre-commit hook**: Runs `pnpm install` if `package.json` changes are staged
traps.why: Describes a hook that exists. Treating a described hook as a control that stops the agent would be a false GATE, and paperfence has already been caught doing the equivalent.
A command table row. No ordering, so not require-before.
A directory table row. Read as scope it fences a path nobody fenced.

traps.quote: These are guidelines, not rigid rules.
traps.why: The document disclaiming its own section. Anything extracted from Task Completion Guidelines as a hard rule contradicts this sentence.
A code sample inside a fenced block.

traps.quote: static isInstance(error: unknown): error is MyError {
traps.why: A 25-line TypeScript sample. Nothing in it is a policy.
